thread:
anya: heads up — customer Montauk just delivered their LoRA weights (v2). Tried a merge into `cust/montauk/lora-final` and seeing a token shift on a handful of conv prompts. low priority but blocking QA sign-off.

samir: can you paste the failing prompt examples?

anya: sure — here's a minimal repro from our smoke set:
```
Prompt: "Summarize quarterly revenue for Q3."
Gold: "Revenue grew 12% YoY driven by ad rev and enterprise deals."
Merged: "Revenue grew 12% YoY driven by ad rev and enterprise deals.\n\n"  <-- extra newline/token boundary
```

eva: that smell like a tokenizer mismatch — Montauk's training config might have used sentencepiece vs our model BPE. check lora metadata for tokenizer field.

anya: confirmed: `lora_metadata.json` has `\"tokenizer\": \"sentencepiece\"`. Our model is `redwood-b1-bpe`. Remapping might be necessary.

denise: we have `tools/token_remap.py` for this, but it only remaps vocab indices for embed_table size parity. Special token order differences can still create offsets. Did you try remapping special tokens explicitly?

anya: I ran remap with default mapping. Still saw offset for <pad>/<eos> ordering. Re-running with explicit special-token map: `python tools/token_remap.py --map-specials montauk_map.json ...`

samir: separate issue: when we quantized the merged weights to int4 the smoke eval showed a big quality hit — hallucinations up. Did you try int8?

anya: kicked off a quick eval pack (200 prompts) to compare FP16 / int8 / int4. Command I used:
```
./bin/run_quick_eval \
  --model artifacts/montauk/merged-v2 \
  --quant int4 \
  --prompts evals/montauk_smoke_200.json \
  --out /tmp/montauk_eval_int4.json
```

deploy-bot: eval job started — job id 98321 — logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/98321/logs

eva: FYI our int4 kernel on this arch has a known fused-layernorm ordering fragility; int8 usually avoids it. Recommend baseline on int8 as a safety step.

anya: preliminary numbers: FP16 baseline (merged) accuracy 0.71, int8 0.69, int4 0.63. Most diffs are around tokenization boundaries and list enumerations. Attaching top-5 diff snippets in the job artifacts.

denise: proposed plan: 1) require tokenizer remap step in the onboarding pipeline when metadata.tokenizer != model.tokenizer; 2) default montauk LoRA to int8 in Dedicated/Private until we validate int4 kernels; 3) add a smoke check that compares tokenized sequences pre/post merge to catch shifts early.

samir: +1 to all. Can we gate merges if the tokenized-seq-diff > 0.5%?

anya: yes — I'll add a lightweight check: `scripts/check_token_shift.py` that returns a diff ratio and make it a pre-merge CI guard. I'll open a PR with remap + check + update to onboarding docs.

denise: also add a short note for SEs: if customer LoRA uses different tokenizer, ask for original tokenizer model or a mapping file. Saves time.

anya: opening PR now. Will re-run smoke eval after remap + int8. ETA EOD PST.

samir: thanks — ping here when the PR is up and when the follow-up eval finishes. :thumbsup:
